peircean_analysis.firstness: SSH brute-force from 185.220.101.47 (Tor exit node) at exact 1-second intervals (02:00:00, 02:00:01, 02:00:02). bash_history: whoami/id/uname-a/wget mimikatz from GitHub/./mimikatz.exe/history -c. exfil.tar.gz: size_bytes=0, MD5=d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e, created=modified=02:03:00Z, permissions 0644. Network: SSH 180 seconds exactly, FTP CONNECTION REFUSED. Cyrillic comments throughout. Auth.log entries with ## comment format.
peircean_analysis.secondness: Every 'Russian APT' indicator contains an internal contradiction: (1) mimikatz.exe on Linux — Windows PE binary, will not execute. (2) Empty exfil file — MD5 d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e is the universally known hash of zero bytes. (3) FTP refused — no exfiltration channel actually worked. (4) 'history -c' in history — self-defeating anti-forensics. (5) Auth.log ## comments — syslog format doesn't support comments. (6) 1-second exact intervals — automated log generation, not real traffic. (7) 180-second exact SSH duration — script precision. (8) APT using public GitHub URL — APTs use private infra. (9) Cyrillic grammar error (обнаружена/обнаружено gender disagreement).
peircean_analysis.thirdness: The 'attack' is entirely theatrical — no data was exfiltrated (empty file, FTP refused), no tools executed successfully (mimikatz on Linux). The entire artifact set is staged evidence designed to implicate Russia. The real actor planted false attribution markers while conducting no actual intrusion impact. The staging itself IS the malicious act: deliberate deception of forensic investigators for false attribution.

hypotheses.H1_genuine_russian_apt: Real Russian APT intrusion with characteristic TTPs — Cyrillic comments, Tor exit node, mimikatz, SSH brute-force.
hypotheses.H2_false_flag_staging: Evidence deliberately staged by a non-Russian actor to create false attribution. Real attacker planted artifacts, conducted no actual exfiltration.

refutation_protocol.benign_hypothesis: H1 (genuine APT): Russian APT groups do use Tor, do use mimikatz, do target SSH. The IP 185.220.101.47 is a known Tor exit node used in multiple attacks.
refutation_protocol.test_result: H1 FULLY REFUTED by four independent internal contradictions: (A) mimikatz.exe cannot execute on Linux — the command in bash_history is inert. (B) exfil.tar.gz is verifiably empty (MD5 of empty file is a known constant — d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e). (C) FTP connection refused — no exfiltration channel existed. (D) 'history -c' appears in the history file it was supposed to clear — logical impossibility. No genuine APT operation contains four self-defeating technical contradictions.
refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: H1 REFUTED. H2 confirmed. The staging IS the MALICE. Eco overinterpretation: evidence too perfectly 'Russian' while being technically incoherent.

devil_advocate: A genuinely incompetent threat actor (script kiddie) could make all these mistakes: download a Windows binary to Linux without realizing it won't run, clear history and forget the command gets recorded, misconfigure FTP. The theatrical Cyrillic comments could be a low-skill actor's attempt at humor rather than professional staging. However: the combination of all these failures simultaneously, with all of them pointing toward attribution while producing zero real impact, exceeds 'incompetence' and enters 'deliberate.' An incompetent actor who downloads mimikatz to Linux still produces impact; a false flagger produces attribution without impact.
eco_overinterpretation_flag: TRIGGERED — evidence is too conveniently 'Russian': four simultaneous theatrical APT markers all of which fail technically. Probability of genuine incompetence producing this specific pattern is negligible. Evidence was staged.
